standard_prerequisites.name: For a finitely generated ideal the derived completion functor is given by the internal Hom from a fixed complex, hence has a right adjoint description
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the completion of the internal Hom into the internal Hom of a tensor product with that fixed complex.

standard_prerequisites.name: The internal Hom satisfies the tensor-hom adjunction, so it can be moved from one argument to the other at the cost of tensoring
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the chain of equalities converting the completion of the Hom of K and L into the Hom of K with the completion of L.

standard_prerequisites.name: The comparison map from a complex to its derived completion is an isomorphism after applying the internal Hom from the completion, by the defining adjunction of the completion
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the second equality, allowing both arguments to be replaced by their completions.

core_obligations: Recall from the author's statement that derived completion is the internal Hom from a fixed complex C, so the completion of the internal Hom of K and L is the internal Hom of C with that same internal Hom (proof lines 26268-26271).

Apply the tensor-hom adjunction to rewrite that expression as the internal Hom of K with the internal Hom of C and L, which is the completion of L; this proves the first equality (proof lines 26272-26276).

For the second equality observe that the map from K to its completion induces a comparison map between the two internal Hom expressions, and that this map is an isomorphism by the defining adjunction of the completion as the left adjoint of the inclusion of derived complete objects (proof lines 26277-26285).
proof_roadmap: Write the completion as an internal Hom (proof lines 26268-26270).
Use the tensor-hom adjunction to move the completion to the second argument (proof lines 26271-26276).
Use the defining adjunction of the completion to allow completing the first argument as well (proof lines 26277-26285).
